full_text: US turns 250: What is the Declaration of Independence? Is it a symbol of freedom or America's greatest paradox? On the US' 250th anniversary, the Declaration of Independence remains fiercely contested over slavery, Indigenous dispossession, constitutional interpretation, and competing narratives like the 1619 Project and the 1776 Commission. Here's why America's founding document continues to shape and divide the nation If you were to believe Hollywood, the United States Declaration of Independence is less a founding political text and more the ultimate high-stakes heist target. When Nicolas Cage’s character, Benjamin Franklin Gates, famously declared in the 2004 cinematic classicNational Treasurethat he was going to steal the Declaration of Independence — complete with invisible ink formulas, Freemason ciphers, and a map drawn on the back byGeorge Washington— it cemented the document in our imagination as a sacred, immutable relic. Yet, as the United States celebrates its Semiquincentennial — its landmark 250th anniversary — this week on July 4, 2026, the reality of the Declaration is far more complex. There is no treasure map on the back of the parchment housed in the National Archives in Washington, DC. But scrawled across its front is a set of ideas that has served as both the architectural blueprint for modern democracy and the focal point of America’s longest-running cultural warfare. Two and a half centuries after a group of wealthy, treasonous colonial elites affixed their signatures to a piece of treated animal skin, the Declaration of Independence remains a paradox: it is an foundational text that proclaimed universal human dignity, written by men who held other human beings in chains. title: Vance pushes back on Vatican's criticism of Trump immigration policies, calls it 'troubling'
full_text: Vance pushes back on Vatican's criticism of Trump immigration policies, calls it 'troubling' US Vice President JD Vance defended the Trump administration's immigration policies, rejecting Pope Leo's criticism of its treatment of migrants while urging Catholic leaders to consider the impact of mass migration US Vice President JD Vance pushed back against Pope Leo’s criticism of the Trump administration’s treatment of migrants, saying he disagreed with the Vatican’s position and stressing that mass migration also creates victims. Speaking in an interview onFox News’The Ingraham Angle, Vance, who is Catholic, responded to Pope Leo’s recent comments on immigration. “I do think that some of the things that have come out of the Vatican on the immigration question in particular have been troubling, and ultimately I disagree with it,”Vance said. He added that he remains open to discussions with Catholic leaders who oppose the administration’s immigration policies. “What I tell the Catholic leadership I talk to who disagree with our immigration policies, you know, I’m not hostile about it. I invite them to have the conversation but I also encourage them to remember that mass migration has victims.” Leo, the first US pope, has called for a “deep reflection” in the United States on the treatment of migrants under the Trump administration. He has described the administration as “extremely disrespectful” towards immigrants and criticised what he called “their inhuman” treatment. President Donald Trump has pursued a hardline immigration crackdown and deportation campaign that rights groups say has violated free speech and due process rights while creating an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities who have expressed concerns about racial profiling.
